paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Everything in this vision starts at the temple, and the water comes from under the threshold. Nobody dug a canal, and nobody hauled it in. The text says it flows because it is "the water from the sanctuary" (Ezekiel 47:12), so life starts at God's own house and runs out from there.

Now watch what that water does to the Dead Sea. The man says that when the river empties into it, "the water there becomes fresh" (Ezekiel 47:8). THE DEAD SEA, friend! The one place nobody expects to see a fishing net. Wherever the river flows, "everything will flourish" (Ezekiel 47:9), and the trees on its banks bear fruit for food and leaves for healing. I know a little about being written off, and I'm telling you, when God brings life, it reaches the places that look finished.

So here's what it means for you, baker. Whatever feels dried up or stuck in your life, God is able to bring His life into it. You don't have to make the river flow yourself, you just stay close to where it comes from. And keep your oven warm, because Ezekiel's vision isn't over yet.
